$comment: This file is the authored source and is not generated. Stable dev-mode warning codes. Each code names exactly one docs page that prevents the mistake, and that page is the code's permanent home. build-tokens.mts emits this file three ways so the runtime, the shipped substrate and the docs cannot drift: OPSIN_ERROR_CODES and OPSIN_ERROR_POLICY in lib/generated/tokens.ts, the OPSIN_ERRORS table inside lib/opsinjs.ts (which warnOnce() reads and which shadcn add copies into a consumer's project), and the generated table under `## How it works` on content/docs/handbook/error-codes.mdx. Edit here; never edit any of the three.

policy.stability: A code is permanent. It is never reused, never renumbered and never removed. A retired code is marked `retired: true` and keeps its row, because the code will outlive this release in somebody's log aggregator.
policy.environment: Warnings are emitted in development only, once per offending call site, through console.warn. Nothing in this list throws, and nothing in this list is emitted in production: a health product must not be made to crash by a documentation-quality complaint.
policy.message: Every message states what was passed, why it is wrong, and the one thing to do instead. A message that only says what is wrong makes the reader search this table, which is a worse version of putting the answer in the message.

severity.safety: A defect that can mislead a reader about their own health. Treat as a bug, not as a lint warning.
severity.correctness: The component will render something, but not what the author meant.
severity.hygiene: Works today, will not survive an upgrade.

codes.title: Both a category and a status were given to one surface
codes.message: <{component}> received both `category="{category}"` and `status="{status}"`. A surface carries one axis. Set the category on the surface and render the status as a StatusPill inside it.

codes.title: A status was rendered without a word
codes.message: <{component}> has `status="{status}"` and no accessible label. Status is carried by colour, icon and word together; colour alone does not survive grayscale, colour-vision deficiency or a black-and-white printout.

codes.title: A value was rendered without a unit
codes.message: <Value> received `{value}` with no `unit`. A bare number in a health context is ambiguous between unit systems: the same digits are one reading in mmol/L and a very different one in mg/dL, and nothing on the surface tells the reader which was meant. Pass the unit the reading was measured in. If the number has no unit by design, such as a composite score, pass `unit={null}` to say so; the warning stays for a caller who simply forgot.

codes.title: A reference range was rendered without a source
codes.message: <{component}> was given a `range` with no `range.source`. Name whose range it is: a laboratory, a device maker, or a clinician. A range is a comparison somebody chose and not a fact about the reader.

codes.title: More than one urgent surface on a screen
codes.message: {count} surfaces on this screen have `status="urgent"`. The escalation budget is one. When everything is urgent, nothing is.

codes.title: A banned word appeared in a component's copy
codes.message: The string "{text}" contains "{word}", which this system does not use. Write "{replacement}" instead.

codes.title: A health value was animated
codes.message: <{component}> is animating a health value with `{token}`. A value that overshoots has displayed, for one frame, a number that is not true. Use `spring-calm`, or render the final value immediately.

codes.title: A raw colour value was passed where a token is required
codes.message: <{component}> received `{prop}="{value}"`. Components take a category or a status, never a colour. A raw value cannot be re-derived for dark mode, for Display-P3, or for a reader who has asked for more contrast.

codes.title: A primitive token was referenced from a component
codes.message: `{token}` is a primitive-tier token. Components consume roles. Primitives may be re-tuned in a minor release; roles are covered by the versioning policy.

codes.title: An unknown category was requested
codes.message: `category="{category}"` is not one of {known}. Adding a category means adding a ramp, not passing a new string.

codes.title: `unknown` was used as a status level
codes.message: `unknown` is the absence of an assertion, not a fifth level. Use it when there is no reading or no range; do not use it to mean 'probably fine'.

codes.title: A trend was drawn from too few points
codes.message: <TrendSparkline> received {count} points and `minimumPoints` is {minimum}. Two readings are not a trend, and drawing one implies a direction the data does not support.

codes.title: A chart's y-axis was truncated
codes.message: <{component}> has `yAxisMin={min}` on a health value. Truncating the axis exaggerates change; a 2% move drawn across the full height of a card reads as a crisis.

codes.title: Category colours were used as chart series colours
codes.message: This chart is colouring {count} series from the category ramps. Category colours identify what a reading is about; using them for series turns an identity into an arbitrary label.

codes.title: A touch target is below the floor
codes.message: <{component}> renders a {width}x{height} hit area. The floor is 44x44, applied to the hit area rather than to the visible box.

codes.title: A stale reading was rendered as current
codes.message: <{component}> was given a reading from {age} ago with no staleness treatment. A number with no time attached is read as 'now'.

codes.title: More than three translucent surfaces are composited
codes.message: {count} translucent material rungs are visible at once; the budget is 3. Beyond three the blur cost is measurable on mid-range devices and the backdrop is unreadable anyway.

codes.title: A deprecated token was referenced
codes.message: `{token}` was deprecated in {version} and is replaced by `{replacement}`. It will be removed in {removal}.

codes.title: The token stylesheet was not loaded
codes.message: `--opsin-tokens-generated` is not set on :root. app/tokens.generated.css has not been imported, or `pnpm run generate` has not run, and every component is falling back to authored defaults.

codes.title: Two theme providers are mounted
codes.message: More than one theme provider is writing the `dark` class. Two providers race on first paint and produce a flash of the wrong theme.

codes.title: A status outside the four levels was passed
codes.message: <{component}> received `status="{status}"`, which is not one of the four levels. The vocabulary is fixed at steady, watch, attention and urgent; a component that accepted a fifth would be inventing a verdict. Nothing was rendered.
